findings.title: Sender check crashes for integrations whose metadata has no sender
findings.body: GitHubInstallation assumes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] always exists when an Integration row exists without an OrganizationIntegration. That is not guaranteed: build_integration in this same provider only sets metadata["sender"] when state contains a sender, so integrations created through the normal pipeline (or older/orphaned integrations whose org link was removed) have no sender key. Re-linking such an installation raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of either proceeding or showing the invalid-installation error page.

findings.title: Token exchange network errors are not handled
findings.body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen outside any try/except (only safe_urlread is wrapped), and get_user_info on line 434 is also invoked without error handling. If GitHub times out, resets the connection, or the /user lookup fails with an exception, the installation pipeline raises an unhandled 500 rather than rendering the github-integration-failed error response that the PR intends for token-exchange failures; only a clean response body lacking access_token/login reaches the graceful path.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the not-found installation path
findings.body: The test now stubs a 404 for /app/installations/{id} but drives the flow with a deliberately wrong state value (ddd023...), so OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-request error before GitHubInstallation/build_integration ever queries the installation. The assertion on "Invalid installation request." passes even if the 404 handling in build_integration ("The GitHub installation could not be found.") is broken or removed, leaving that branch untested under the new two-step pipeline.
